               <ns0:p n="7">7 Now I pray to God that ye do no evil <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">I do not desire that when I come I may find Objects for my severity, (upon whom I may shew a proof of <ns0:hi>Chri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> in me,</ns0:hi> by exercising that authority upon them, with which Christ hath <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>rusted me) no, on the contrary I heartily pray that ye may be holy and blameless, <ns0:hi>without spot or wrinkler.</ns0:hi> Neither do I desire this for my own sake, that I may be <ns0:hi>approved,</ns0:hi> but I singly desire it for your good</ns0:note>, not that we should appear approved <ns0:hi>r,</ns0:hi> but that ye should do that which is honest, though <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 6.9.</ns0:note> we be as repro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bates <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">that you may do that is good; and then do you, and let the World think of me as a Reprobate, or what they will.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">Truth in this place notes <ns0:hi>integrity of life</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>conversation; truth</ns0:hi> in action, opposed to Hypocrisy, or scandalous living. He had before prayed, that <ns0:hi>they might do no Evil</ns0:hi>; which if they did not, they need not fea<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> his coming with <ns0:hi>a rod</ns0:hi>; for though he had a power from Christ to punish, yet he had no power to punish such as did well; his power was to be used for them, not against them. As the <ns0:hi>Law was not made for the righteous,</ns0:hi> and the Civil Magistrate is not ordained of God for the terrour of those that do well, but only of those that do evil: So neither did Christ ever ordain Ecclesiastical Censures for the punishment, of good and holy men. And indeed here is the just boundary of all <ns0:hi>Civil</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ecclesiastical power</ns0:hi>; No Magistrate or Minister, acting as Christs Servants <ns0:hi>can</ns0:hi> (lawfully, or as by any Commissi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on from him) do any thing <ns0:hi>against the truth,</ns0:hi> or those that owne, defend, and practise it; the power, with which they are be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trusted, is for <ns0:hi>edification,</ns0:hi> not <ns0:hi>destruction.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 For we are glad <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 4.10. C<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>p. 11.30. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 12.5, 9, 10.</ns0:note> when we are weak <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Some by <ns0:hi>Weakness</ns0:hi> here understand, a moral impotency; as the Apostle had said, <ns0:hi>he could not do any thing against the truth,</ns0:hi> that is rightly and justly he could not.</ns0:note>, and ye are strong <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">And by <ns0:hi>strong</ns0:hi> here, a spiritual strength, a reformation, growth, and profici<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ency in grace. These make the sence to be this; I am so far from coming with a desire to shew amongst you my Apostolical power in punishing offenders, as that I should be glad to find you so <ns0:hi>strong</ns0:hi> in the exercise of grace, that I should find none to punish; that men be made <ns0:hi>weak</ns0:hi> (as to the putting forth that power) by your spiritual strength. I incline to a more general interpretation. The Apostle by this purgeth himself from any thing of Vain-glory, or seeking himself; <ns0:hi>Though</ns0:hi> saith he) <ns0:hi>I be weak,</ns0:hi> (as some amongst you report me) yet if you be truly <ns0:hi>strong,</ns0:hi> I shall heartily rejoice therein.</ns0:note>: and this also we wish, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> your perfection <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">For I wish nothing more than <ns0:hi>your perfection</ns0:hi>; my reputation is nothing to me com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pared with that.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 <ns0:note place="margin">
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> Cor. 4.21. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 2.3. & <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.2 & 12. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 11.</ns0:note> Therefore I write these things being ab<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sent, lest being present, I should use sharpness, according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">The Apostle here lets them know with how much tender<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness he dealt with them; and whereas they might have charged him with sharpness in his Letters, he assures them, that he therefore had so wrote, that he might prevent sharper dealings with them when he should come to them; by their hearkening to the admonitions of his Letter; For otherwise he tells them, that after he came he must deal more sharply with them in the execution of that power with which Christ had betrusted him. Yet he further tells them, that that power was for their good, not for their harm; for their <ns0:hi>edification,</ns0:hi> not for their <ns0:hi>destructi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on</ns0:hi>; (which is the same with what he had said, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 10.8. and in the Verse immediately preceding.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 Finally, brethren, farewel <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">The Apostle shutteth up his Epistle according to the or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dinary form of Conclusions of Letters, wishing all happiness to them.</ns0:note>: Be perfect <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">But he addeth something as a Christian, and a Mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nister of the Gospel: <ns0:hi>Be ye perfect</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> The word <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
signifies to be compact, or united, as members of the same bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dy, or parts of the same house; the perfection of a Society ly<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing much in the union of it. The <ns0:hi>Perfection</ns0:hi> the Apostle pres<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />seth here, seemeth to be the <ns0:hi>perfection of the body</ns0:hi> of the Church, by the restoring of such as were separated from its Communion, or had, through a Spirit of contention, withdrawn themselves, rather than the <ns0:hi>perfection</ns0:hi> of the particular Members of it, in the habits and exercises of Grace. The <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> word seemeth that way to carry the sense; it properly signifies, the putting of members loosed from their joynts into their proper place a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gain, and such a perfection as followeth upon such an action, or any action proportionable to it.</ns0:note>, be of good comfort <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">The word imports <ns0:hi>Ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />horted, comforted, confirmed:</ns0:hi> Be <ns0:hi>exhorted</ns0:hi> to yield obedience to my precepts, or counsels; be <ns0:hi>comforted</ns0:hi> in all the trials or afflictions you do meet with, or may further meet with, for your profession of the Gospel; be <ns0:hi>confirmed</ns0:hi> in the truths and holy ways of God.</ns0:note>, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rom. 12.16. 1 Cor. 1.10. 1 Pet. 3.8</ns0:note> be of one mind <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Be of one mind,</ns0:hi> if possible, of one and the same judgment in the Truths of God; however, as pursu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing the same scope and end; be one in affection.</ns0:note>, live in peace <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Live in peace,</ns0:hi> free from those contentions and divisions, those debates, and stri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>es, and wraths, and envyings, which I have before told you of as faults among you.</ns0:note>; and the God of love and peace shall be with you <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">This is the way for to have the presence of God with you, for he is not the God of hatred and strife, but the <ns0:hi>God of Love</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Peace</ns0:hi>; who hath command<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed Love and Peace amongst those that are Brethren, and will be present among them only who live in obedience to his Royal Law of Love.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Thes. 5.26. 1 Pet. 5.14.</ns0:note> Greet one another with an holy kiss <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">See the Notes on <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 16.16. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 16.20. 'Twas an ancient custom and of common use, when Friends met, for them (as a token of mutual Love and Friendship) to kiss each other: The Christians use it also at their Ecclesiastical Assemb<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lings: It must not be lookt upon as a Precept, obliging all Chri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stians to do the like; but only as directing those that then did use it, to use it innocently, chastly, sincerely and holily.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 All the Saints salute you <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">That is, all about me in these parts of <ns0:hi>Macedonia,</ns0:hi> wish you all happiness; and by me send the remembrance of their love and respects to you.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">The free love of our Lord Jesus Christ, shews in the appli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cation of his Redemption; that grace which floweth from him as the Fountain of Grace, or cometh by him as the Mediator, between God and Man.</ns0:note>, and the love of God <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The actual <ns0:hi>love of God,</ns0:hi> that good will by which God the Father imbraceth Creatures in Christ, and for his sake</ns0:note>, and the communion of the holy Ghost <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> with you all <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">And all the gracious Communications of the holy Spirit of God, (by which he strengtheneth, quickeneth, or comforteth the Souls of Gods People) <ns0:hi>be with all of you.</ns0:hi> Whether you value me or no, I heartily wish you well, and all the best things. In this Text, is an eminent proof of the <ns0:hi>Tri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nity</ns0:hi>; all the persons being distinctly named in it, (as in the Commission about Baptism.) The Apostle calleth the Father, <ns0:hi>God</ns0:hi>; the Son, <ns0:hi>Lord:</ns0:hi> He attributeth <ns0:hi>Love</ns0:hi> to the <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi>; (mo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ved by which he sent his only begotten Son into the World, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 3 16.) <ns0:hi>Grace</ns0:hi> to the Son, who loved us freely, and dyed for the Fellowship, or <ns0:hi>Communion</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Holy Ghost,</ns0:hi> by whom the <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Son</ns0:hi> communicate their love and grace to the Saints.</ns0:note>. <ns0:hi>Amen</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Amen</ns0:hi> is here used as a Particle of wishing or desiring the thing before-mentioned; 'tis the same with, <ns0:hi>Let it so be.</ns0:hi> Whether added by the Apostle, or subjoined by the Church of <ns0:hi>Corinth,</ns0:hi> upon the reading this <ns0:hi>Epistle</ns0:hi> amongst them, (as some think) is not material.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

                  <ns0:head>¶ The second Epistle to the Corinthians, was written from Philippi a City of Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cedonia, by Titus and Lucas.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p>If the Subscriptions to the Apostolical Epistles were parts of the Text and holy Writ, we have it here determined, who that other Brother was, mentioned <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 8.22. sent along with <ns0:hi>Titus</ns0:hi> to carry this Letter, and the benevolence of the Churches of <ns0:hi>Macedonia.</ns0:hi> But it is observed, that even in this Subscription there is a certain evidence, that the Subscriptions of the Epistles are no part of <ns0:hi>Canonical Writ</ns0:hi>; for in some <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> Copies it is said to be sent by <ns0:hi>Paul,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Timothy</ns0:hi>; whereas <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> was the Writer of it<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> not the Messenger, and in <ns0:hi>Macedonia</ns0:hi> when it was sent; and <ns0:hi>Timothy</ns0:hi> is joined with him in the writing, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 1.1.</ns0:p>
